January 14 3.

CONFIDENTIAL

Dear Mr. Van den Berg,

With reference to your note of December 28, 1932,
Albert M. Suptil is an American subject described as
a free-lance journalist. He arrived in Shanghai in
1924 and soon afterwards obtained employment as a
reporter with the "Shanghai Times". He remained there
only for a short time owing to his weakness for liquor.
During 1925 and 1926 he was employed in the Commercial
Office of the United States Consulate, but lost this
position through heavy drinking. He was then unemployed
until 1928 when he was appointed local manager of
Mathieson & Alkali Inc., American Manufacturing Chemists.
After leaving this firm, Suptil has been at various times
employed with the Shanghai Evening Post and the Mercury
Press. Suptil, who is heavily in debt, is at present
staying at the Ahung Lodge Hotel (亚亨旅馆), Nanking
Road (N.R.).

Yours faithfully,

（签名）

2. For the Registrar,
American Consulate-General.

机密

亲爱的范登伯格先生：

关于您1932年12月28日的便函，阿尔伯特·M·苏普蒂尔（Albert M. Suptil）系美国籍臣民，自称自由撰稿记者。他于1924年抵达上海，不久后受雇于《字林西报》（Shanghai Times）担任记者。由于嗜酒成性，他仅在该报工作了很短时间。1925年至1926年间，他在美国领事馆商务办事处任职，但因酗酒严重而失去该职位。此后他一直失业，直到1928年被任命为美国制造化学家麦基森与罗宾斯公司（McKesson & Robbins Inc.，注：此处原文为Mathieson & Alkali Inc.，但下文报告及常识指向McKesson，依下文报告修正或保留原文疑点，此处依下文p3更正为McKesson & Robbins，但本段原文写的是Mathieson，故忠实翻译原文）的马西森与碱业公司（Mathieson & Alkali Inc.）本地经理。离开该公司后，苏普蒂尔曾断续受雇于《上海晚邮报》（Shanghai Evening Post）和墨丘利出版社（Mercury Press）。苏普蒂尔负债累累，目前住在南京路（N.R.）的亚亨旅馆（Ahung Lodge Hotel）。

此致
敬礼，

（签名）

Date: January 17, 1933.

Subject (in full)........................................................ Enquiry re: A.M. Guptil.

Made by .................... and ................................ Forwarded by .................... D.S.I. Moore.

Reference attached memorandum from the Netherlands
Consulate-General. The person in question is Albert M. Guptil
an American subject, who describes himself as a Free-lance
Journalist. He arrived in Shanghai sometime in 1924 and ob-
tained employment as a reporter with the "Shanghai Times", his
services being terminated after a short while owing to his
weakness for liquor. During 1925 and 1926 he was employed in
the Commercial Office, United States Consulate, in a clerical
capacity, his drinking habits putting a stop to this position,
and for while he was unemployed. During 1928 Guptil was ap-
pointed local manager for McKesson & Robbins Inc., America
Manufacturing Chemists, but his drinking bouts again termina-
ted this appointment, and since, other short-lived periods of
employment have been with the Shanghai Evening Post, and the
Mercury Press.
He is heavily in debt, and is at present staying at
the Chin Loong Hotel, (金龍寄宿舍) off Woosung Road (O.O.I.).

D. S. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

DECEMBER 24, 1932 THE CHINESE REPUBLIC 842

SUGGESTION FOR CO-OPERATION BETWEEN S.M.C.
AND CHINESE AREAS

Indications are pointing to an understanding
being reached between the authorities of Greater
Shanghai and the Shanghai Telephone Company,
with sanction of the Shanghai Municipal Coun-
cil, over the disputed matter of telephone ser-
vice upon municipal council owned roads locat-
ed outside the limits of the International Settle-
ment and in Chapei areas adjoining those roads.
Further indications point to some sort of a
working agreement being on the point of cul-
mination with respect to police authority upon
these disputed highways, at present a veritable
no-man's land with Chinese and foreign con-
trolled police organizations both functioning
but imperfectly upon them with residents there-
on dissatisfied and neither party to the dispute
quite sure of itself.

With these longstanding arguments almost
settled, it now seems opportune to revive a sug-
gestion made as far back as 1923 by a distin-
guished member of the Consular Body, a sug-
gestion which if carried to its logical conclusion
eventually would settle the question of the
future status of Shanghai to the satisfaction of
everyone concerned, a program which could not
help but remove the age old causes of friction
between the foreign controlled areas and ad-
jacent Chinese administered districts all of which
go to comprise the real Greater Shanghai.

Radical Change Of Policy Advocated

It was in the summer of 1923 that the con-
sular official whose name cannot yet be disclosed
granted an interview in which he inspired a
magazine article wherein was advocated a then
radical change of policy on the part of the ad-
ministrations of the two foreign controlled areas
at Shanghai. As he pointed out at the time,
and is still pertinent, the underlying cause of
Chapei's backwardness as compared with the
development of the International Settlement
and the French Concession is lack of adequate
revenue. It is all very well for the prideful
foreigner to invite an odious comparison be-
tween his well kept municipalities and the shabby
Chinese administered areas adjacent thereto. But
is it fair for the foreigner to make this com-
parison? At least one important foreign official
believes not. And why?

By A. M. GUPTIL

In the first place, due to a whim of nature,
aided and abetted by foreign controlled customs
and conservancy services, the bulk of Shang-
hai's trade has to pass through the International
Settlement. Artificial stimulants, the greatest
of them being a sense of security within the
bounds of the settlement, have packed that area
with business houses and offices. Land values
have appreciated to a remarkable extent as com-
pared with those prevailing in Chapei and
other Chinese districts and revenues have kept
pace. The result has been that where the
Shanghai Municipal Council might find a mil-
lion dollars to spend on road work, the authori-
ties in Chapei, for instance, might be hard put
to raise ten thousand for similar purposes.

It was proposed in 1923 that this discre-
pancy in taxable values be recognized by the
governments of the French Concession and the
International Settlement. It was further sug-
gested that the two councils make a flat admis-
sion of the essential indivisibility of the Chinese
and foreign areas which together comprise
Greater Shanghai. And it was stated to be a
bounden duty on the part of the foreign councils
to recognize their financial responsibilities with
regard to their Chinese neighbors and arrange in
the most convenient and equitable manner pos-
sible to attain for a substantial admission of that
responsibility in the form of financial support
to the Chinese administered section of Greater
Shanghai.

Not so far fetched as it seems at first glance
is this proposal. Rather than being the idea of
a flighty visionary is it the result of years of
close study on the part of a particularly hard
headed individual whose business it is to deal in
facts and whom emotion sways not all. So let
us see what is proposed as a program of progress
for this metropolis. It is simplicity in itself.

A Council Of Mixed Members

Let negotiations be undertaken through the
medium of a super Municipal Council, a body
with no standing at all in law but composed of
members of the councils of the several areas in-
volved. Let this body promise its deliberations
and recommendations to its respective legal

1932年12月24日 《中华民国》 842期

关于工部局与中国辖区合作的建议

有迹象表明，在上海公共租界工部局的批准下，大上海当局与上海电话公司之间，就位于国际租界界限之外且毗邻闸北地区的工部局所属道路上的电话服务这一争议事项，正达成谅解。进一步的迹象表明，关于这些争议道路上的警察管辖权问题，某种工作协议即将达成；目前这些道路实际上是无人管辖地带，中国和外国控制的警察组织虽都在此运作，但效果不佳，当地居民对此不满，且争议双方均无十足把握。

随着这些长期争论几乎得到解决，现在似乎是重提一位领事团杰出成员早在1923年提出的建议的适当时机。该建议若按其逻辑贯彻到底，最终将令所有相关方满意地解决上海未来地位的问题，这一方案无疑将消除外国控制区与相邻中国管辖区（两者共同构成真正的大上海）之间长期存在的摩擦根源。

倡导政策的根本改变

1923年夏，一位姓名尚不便披露的领事官员接受了一次采访，他在采访中启发了一篇杂志文章，文中主张当时上海两个外国控制区的行政当局进行一项激进的政策改变。正如他当时指出且至今仍然切中要害的那样，闸北相对于国际租界和法租界的发展而言之所以落后，其根本原因是缺乏足够的财政收入。傲慢的外国人将其管理良好的市政区域与相邻的破旧中国管辖区进行令人反感的对比，这固然容易，但这种对比对外国人来说公平吗？至少有一位重要的外国官员认为不公平。原因何在？

作者：A. M. 古普蒂尔（A. M. GUPTIL）

首先，由于自然的偶然因素，并在外国控制的海关和浚浦局的推波助澜下，上海的大部分贸易必须通过国际租界。人为的刺激因素，其中最大的是租界范围内的安全感，使得该地区挤满了商行和办公室。与闸北和其他中国地区普遍流行的地价相比，这里的土地价值显著升值，财政收入也随之增长。结果是，当上海公共租界工部局可能找到一百万美元用于道路工程时，例如闸北当局可能很难筹集一万美元用于类似目的。

1923年提出的建议是，法租界和国际租界的政府应承认这种应税价值的差异。进一步建议两个公董局公开承认，组成大上海的中国区域和外国区域在本质上是不可分割的。并指出，外国公董局有义务承认其对邻近中国区域的财政责任，并以尽可能方便和公平的方式安排，以实质性地承认这一责任，形式上是对大上海中国管辖区提供财政支持。

这一提议并不像乍看之下那样牵强附会。它并非一个轻率的空想家的想法，而是一个特别务实的人多年深入研究的结果，此人的工作是处理事实，不受情感左右。那么，让我们看看为大都市提出的进步方案是什么。它本身很简单。

混合成员委员会

让谈判通过一个超级市政委员会进行，该机构在法律上没有任何地位，但由所涉及各个区域的公董局成员组成。让该机构基于以下假设向其各自的法定机构提交审议结果和建议：在未来许多年里，如果试图迫使中国区域沿现代化路线发展，以达到或至少接近租界和公租界所显示的进步水平，上海的中国区域将无法自给自足。让该机构公开并一劳永逸地承认，上海不仅仅是两个租界和一个中国贫民窟。让它承认闸北和南市对租界的必要性，正如租界对中国区域一样，并让相关的公董局承认其在维护秩序、公共卫生和推进公共工程方面的共同责任。简而言之，让外国人表现出希望以整体方式而非过去那种零敲碎打的方式援助这个港口发展的愿望。让外国公董局拨出一定比例的财政收入，用于中国区域的公共工程、公共卫生、警察等事务。从金钱角度来看，这将是一项值得的投资，因为人们怀疑，一旦中国居民和当局确信此类安排的诚意和永久性，目前大部分的反外情绪就会随之消失。毕竟，是中国的资金建设并维持着租界和公租界。当其中一部分资金花在中国领土上时，中国人的情绪将会改变。此外，在上述采访中有人问道，为何不安排租界和公租界官员与中国区域进行交换，可能作为联络官，以促进这些机构之间的更好理解。在某些情况下，外国行政当局很可能从中国区域官员的经验中受益。同样，中国行政当局也可能欢迎外国市政官员对其问题提供帮助和建议，而此事的人性化一面，即在相关行政机构之间培养更好的感情，将是促成此类安排的最大动力。
为何不推动真正的大上海的发展？为何不以合作的精神着手解决这个问题，决心使上海成为真正的东方大都市，一个伟大的现代商业中心，每个利益相关者都接受其对整体的责任，与其伙伴共同承担负担，而不是像目前经常发生的那样各自为政？随着电话和道路问题的解决，建设性政治艺术的真正机会邀请我们思考和行动。

SUGGESTION FOR CO-OPERATION
(Continued from Page 149)
bodies upon the assumption that for many years
to come the Chinese districts of Shanghai will
not be self supporting in the event of attempts
being made to force their development along
modern lines to equal or at least to approximate
the progress shown by the concession and the
settlement. Let this body admit in public, once
and for all that Shanghai is more than two
settlements and a Chinese slum district. Let it
admit the necessity of Chapei and Nantao to
the settlements as the latter are to the Chinese
areas and let the councils interested admit their
joint responsibility for the preservation of order,
public health and the furtherance of public
works. In short, let the foreigners evidence a
desire to aid in the development of this port as
a whole, rather than in the piecemeal manner of
the past. Let the foreign councils apportion
a definite percentage of their revenues to be ex-
pended upon public works, public health, police
and the like in the Chinese areas. It would be
an investment well worth making in terms of
dollars and cents for one suspects that once the
Chinese residents and authorities became con-
vinced of the sincerity and permanence of such
an arrangement, right then and there would the
greater part of present anti-foreign sentiment
disappear. For it is Chinese money that
has built and is keeping the concession and the
settlement. When some of it is spent in Chin-
ese territory, Chinese sentiment will change.
And, it was asked in the interview referred
to, why not arrange an exchange of concession
and settlement officers with the Chinese areas,
as liason officers probably, to promote a better
understanding between these bodies. It is more
than probable that in some instances the foreign
administrations would benefit by the experience
of officials in the Chinese districts. It is like-
wise possible that a Chinese administration
would welcome the assistance and advice of for-
eign municipal officers upon their problems,
while the human side of the matter, the
engendering of better feeling between the ad-
ministrative bodies concerned would be the
greatest of incentives to such an arrangement.
Why not push forward development of a
real Greater Shanghai. Why not tackle the
problem in a spirit of get together, with deter-
mination to make Shanghai the real metropolis
of the Orient, a great, modern commercial
center with every interest accepting its respon-
sibility toward the whole, bearing its share of
the burden in common with its fellow rather
than working at cross purposes as is all too often
the case at present? The telephones and the
roads out of the way, the real opportunity for
constructive statesmanship invites thought and
action.

I. O. CENTRAL Station.

January 31 1925

REPORT ON Search for Albert M. Guptil by request of
American Consular Authorities.

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by J. Givens A. I.

Sir,

Albert M. Guptil employed in the commercial
office of the American Consulate who has been missing
for the past three days, went into the General Hospital
at 6 p.m. January 30. He is in a first class ward and
is being attended by Dr. Bryson. I gathered from the
demeanour of the office sister from whom I made inquiries
that Guptil has entered the hospital to cover up his
indiscretions. Mr. Jacobs has been notified of Guptil's
whereabouts.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. Ludeman.
D. I.

D. C. I.

中央巡捕房情报官。

1925年1月31日

关于应美国领事当局要求搜寻阿尔伯特·M·古普蒂尔（Albert M. Guptil）的报告。

由侦探督察沙利文（D. I. Sullivan）制作，由助理督察吉文斯（J. Givens A. I.）转呈。

先生，

在美国领事馆商务办事处任职的阿尔伯特·M·古普蒂尔已失踪三天，他于1月30日下午6点进入广慈医院（General Hospital）。他住在一等病房，由布莱森医生（Dr. Bryson）诊治。我从向其查询的护士长举止中得知，古普蒂尔入院是为了掩盖其不当行为。雅各布斯先生（Mr. Jacobs）已获知古普蒂尔的下落。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J. 卢德曼（J. Ludeman）。
侦探督察（D. I.）
